2 Model Structure

yield_tha ~ landscape heterogeneity (swf) + intrinsic variaton + field design

Because the surrounding-landscape predictor is a curve rather than a single number, the response is modelled with a scalar-on-function regression (refund::pfr), which is a generalized additive model (mgcv) extended to accept functional covariates.

This document analyses crop yield (yield_tha) in an agroforestry system as a function of three groups of predictors:

  1. surrounding landscape - the proportion of small woody features (SWF) around the field, expressed as a function of distance from the field boundary (100-1000 m, 100 m steps);
  2. intrinsic variation - the distance from the sampled plot to the tree strip within the field;
  3. field design - fixed characteristics of each field/year (climate, soil, landscape configuration, crop, tree age, planting year).

Because the surrounding-landscape predictor is a curve rather than a single number, the response is modelled with a scalar-on-function regression (refund::pfr), which is a generalized additive model (mgcv) extended to accept functional covariates.

The data-exploration section below follows the structure recommended by Zuur et al. 2010: - outlier - distribution/homogeneity of the response - zero-inflation - collinearity - relationships - independence of observations.

df <- read.csv("C:/Users/Elizaveta/OneDrive - Universität Bayreuth/Dokumente/MasterThesis/MA_RProject/data/AnalysisData/20260819_AFswf.csv")

df <- df |>
  mutate(year_AFplanting = case_when(
    field == "Dornburg"      ~ 2007,
    field == "Forst"         ~ 2010,
    field == "Gladbacherhof" ~ 2020,
    field == "IhingerHof"    ~ 2008,
    field == "Mariensee"     ~ 2008,
    field == "Reiffenhausen" ~ 2011,
    field == "Vechta"        ~ 2019,
    field == "Wendhausen"    ~ 2008
  ))

fert_raw <- gsub("[\u2013\u2212]", "-", df$fertilization_rate_kg_n_p_k_ha_1_year_1)
df$fert_N <- as.numeric(sub("^([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", fert_raw))
df$fert_N[fert_raw == "no fertilization"] <- 0

# one row per plot-year observation, for exploration of scalar variables
base_explore <- df |>
  distinct(id, field, year, yield_tha, distance_to_tree_strip,
           crop_unified, area, fert_N, temp_C_mean, sun_MJ_m2_mean,
           precip_mm_sum, l_shdi, l_contag, l_ed, l_ai,
           mean_slope, min_slope, max_slope, treeage,
           year_AFplanting, prop_swf_within)

3 Data Exploration

3.1 Distribution of the response variable: yield tha

ggplot(df, aes(x = seq_along(yield_tha), y = yield_tha)) +
  geom_point(shape = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Observation",
    y = "Yield (t/ha)"
  )

ggplot(df, aes(x = seq_along(yield_tha), y = yield_tha, color = crop_unified)) +
  geom_point(shape = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Observation",
    y = "Yield (t/ha)"
  )

ggplot(df, aes(x = seq_along(yield_tha), y = yield_tha, color = distance_to_tree_strip)) +
  geom_point(shape = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Observation",
    y = "Yield (t/ha)"
  )

3.2 Outliers

Cleveland dotplots for every continuous variable (observation order on the y-axis, value on the x-axis) make isolated extreme values easy to spot without imposing a distributional assumption.

num_vars <- c("yield_tha", "distance_to_tree_strip", "fert_N",
              "temp_C_mean", "sun_MJ_m2_mean", "precip_mm_sum",
              "l_shdi", "l_contag", "l_ed", "l_ai",
              "mean_slope", "treeage", "prop_swf_within")

dotplot_data <- base_explore |>
  select(all_of(num_vars)) |>
  mutate(row = row_number()) |>
  pivot_longer(-row, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value")

ggplot(dotplot_data, aes(x = value, y = row)) +
  geom_point(shape = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "observation order", x = NULL,
       title = "Cleveland dotplots for outlier screening")

Flag anything that sits noticeably apart from the bulk of the points in its panel; decide case by case whether it is a data-entry error (fix), a genuine extreme value (keep, but check its influence on the fitted model later), or an artefact of the extraction pipeline (e.g. a boundary raster cell with no woody-cover pixels).

3.3 Distribution / homogeneity of the response

ggplot(base_explore, aes(x = yield_tha)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, colour = "white") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of yield_tha")

ggplot(base_explore, aes(x = crop_unified, y = yield_tha)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "yield_tha by crop", x = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

yield_tha differs strongly by crop (as the boxplot and the model’s parametric coefficients confirm), which is why crop_unified is kept as a fixed factor rather than pooled. Within-crop spread should look roughly comparable across fields/years for a Gaussian pfr to be an appropriate choice; strong heteroscedasticity by crop would motivate a weights = argument or a variance-modelling approach.

3.4 Zero-inflation

sapply(base_explore[num_vars], function(x) mean(x == 0, na.rm = TRUE))
##              yield_tha distance_to_tree_strip                 fert_N 
##             0.00000000             0.00000000             0.34621329 
##            temp_C_mean         sun_MJ_m2_mean          precip_mm_sum 
##             0.00000000             0.00000000             0.00000000 
##                 l_shdi               l_contag                   l_ed 
##             0.00000000             0.00000000             0.00000000 
##                   l_ai             mean_slope                treeage 
##             0.00000000             0.00000000             0.16567037 
##        prop_swf_within 
##             0.01736614

None of the continuous predictors or the response should show a disproportionate spike at zero (fert_N is expected to have a genuine, meaningful cluster at 0 for “no fertilization” plots - that is not zero-inflation in the statistical sense, just a real category, and is handled by the smooth term being able to flatten out near 0).

Pay particular attention to area, mean_slope, min_slope, max_slope, temp_C_mean, sun_MJ_m2_mean, precip_mm_sum, l_shdi, l_contag, l_ed, l_ai - with only 8 fields, several of these are near-constant within a field and therefore highly correlated with field identity itself (see Section 5.3, concurvity). area and mean_slope/min_slope/max_slope are dropped from the model for exactly this reason: each has a single value per field.

3.6 Relationships between yield and candidate predictors

rel_data <- base_explore |>
  select(yield_tha, distance_to_tree_strip, fert_N, temp_C_mean,
         precip_mm_sum, l_shdi, treeage, crop_unified) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(yield_tha, crop_unified), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value")

ggplot(rel_data, aes(x = value, y = yield_tha)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ crop_unified + variable, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw()

df |>
  select(id, distance, prop_swf) |>
  distinct() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = distance, y = prop_swf)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "prop_swf as a function of distance from the field boundary")

Loess curves that are clearly non-straight (as expected for distance_to_tree_strip and for prop_swf vs. distance) are the empirical justification for modelling these relationships with penalized smooths / a functional term rather than linear terms.

3.7 Independence of observations

table(base_explore$field)
## 
##      Dornburg         Forst Gladbacherhof    IhingerHof     Mariensee 
##           226            64           144           480            48 
## Reiffenhausen        Vechta    Wendhausen 
##            24            73           112
base_explore |> count(field, year) |> tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n)
## # A tibble: 8 × 9
##   field         `2016` `2017` `2018` `2019` `2020` `2021` `2022` `2023`
##   <chr>          <int>  <int>  <int>  <int>  <int>  <int>  <int>  <int>
## 1 Dornburg          16     16     16     32     30     40     40     36
## 2 Forst             16     16     NA     16     16     NA     NA     NA
## 3 Gladbacherhof     NA     NA     NA     NA     NA    144     NA     NA
## 4 IhingerHof        90     NA    102     NA     NA    100     88    100
## 5 Mariensee         NA     24     24     NA     NA     NA     NA     NA
## 6 Reiffenhausen     12     12     NA     NA     NA     NA     NA     NA
## 7 Vechta            NA     NA     NA     12     13     16     16     16
## 8 Wendhausen        16     16     NA     16     16     16     16     16

Multiple plots per field and multiple years per field mean observations are not independent at the field level (and possibly the plot level across years). This nesting is why the model includes s(field, bs = "re") rather than treating all 647 rows as independent replicates; if a given id/plot recurs across years, consider adding a plot-level random effect as well (see Section 5.5).

4 Variable Overview

Variable Description Unit Role in model
yield_tha Crop yield t/ha Scalar response
W_swf (built from distance, prop_swf) Proportion of small woody features (SWF) in the annulus at each distance from the field boundary proportion (0-1), function of distance (m) Functional predictor (continuous), entered via lf()
distance_to_tree_strip Distance from the sampled plot to the nearest agroforestry tree strip m Continuous scalar predictor, smooth term
prop_swf_within Proportion of SWF inside the field’s own circular footprint (radius = boundary_min) proportion (0-1) Continuous scalar predictor (field design context; consider as smooth or covariate)
crop_unified Harmonised crop type grown that year category (7 levels: grass, maize, potato, rapeseed, rye, wheat, …) Categorical predictor, parametric factor
area Field area m^2 (or ha, check source) Field design - dropped (1 unique value per field, confounded with field RE)
fert_N Nitrogen fertilization rate (parsed from the N-P-K string; “no fertilization” = 0) kg N ha^-1 yr^-1 Continuous scalar predictor, smooth term
temp_C_mean Mean growing-season temperature deg C Continuous scalar predictor, smooth term
sun_MJ_m2_mean Mean solar radiation MJ/m^2 Continuous scalar predictor, smooth term
precip_mm_sum Total precipitation mm Continuous scalar predictor, smooth term
l_shdi Shannon diversity index of the surrounding landscape (FRAGSTATS) index Continuous scalar predictor, smooth term
l_contag Contagion index of the surrounding landscape index Continuous scalar predictor, smooth term
l_ed Edge density of the surrounding landscape m/ha Continuous scalar predictor, smooth term
l_ai Aggregation index of the surrounding landscape index Continuous scalar predictor, smooth term
mean_slope, min_slope, max_slope Field topographic slope statistics degrees Field design - mean_slope dropped (1 value per field, confounded with field RE); min_slope/max_slope currently unused, candidates for the same treatment
treeage Age of the agroforestry tree strip in the given year years Continuous scalar predictor, smooth term
year_AFplanting Year the agroforestry system was planted at that field year (categorical, 8 levels, 1 per field) Field design - candidate for factor()/smooth; near-collinear with field
field Field identifier category (8 levels) Random-effect grouping factor, s(field, bs = "re")
id Unique plot-year observation identifier - Row/observation key, not a covariate
year Calendar year of observation year Available for a year effect / repeated-measures structure, not currently in the model
distance Distance from field boundary at which prop_swf was measured m (100-1000, step 100) Domain (argvals) of the functional predictor W_swf, not a covariate itself

5 Model Specification

5.1 Building the functional covariate

prop_swf is recorded at 10 fixed distances (100-1000 m, 100 m steps) per id. Pivoting to wide format gives one row per id and one column per distance - this matrix is the discretised functional predictor W_swf(distance), and grid is its domain.

W_swf <- df |>
  dplyr::select(id, distance, swf_year, prop_swf) |>
  unique() |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = distance, values_from = prop_swf) |>
  arrange(id)

id_order <- W_swf$id
W_mat    <- as.matrix(W_swf[, -c(1, 2)])
grid     <- as.numeric(colnames(W_mat))

stopifnot(!anyNA(grid), length(grid) == ncol(W_mat))

5.2 Building the scalar dataset

One row per id, aligned exactly to the row order of W_mat.

base <- df |>
  distinct(id, field, year, yield_tha, distance_to_tree_strip,
           crop_unified, area, fert_N, temp_C_mean, sun_MJ_m2_mean,
           precip_mm_sum, l_shdi, l_contag, l_ed, l_ai,
           mean_slope, min_slope, max_slope, treeage,
           year_AFplanting, prop_swf_within) |>
  filter(id %in% id_order) |>
  slice(match(id_order, id))

stopifnot(nrow(base) == nrow(W_mat))
base$W_swf <- W_mat

base$field         <- factor(base$field)
base$crop_unified  <- factor(base$crop_unified)

5.3 Adaptive basis dimensions

safe_k() caps every smooth’s basis dimension (k) at (number of unique values - 1) of its own covariate, so that smooth.construct can never fail regardless of how listwise deletion (NAs anywhere in the formula) thins the fitting sample.

safe_k <- function(x, k_wanted) {
  min(k_wanted, length(unique(x[!is.na(x)])) - 1)
}

k_dist  <- safe_k(base$distance_to_tree_strip, 6)
k_fertN <- safe_k(base$fert_N,                 5)
k_temp  <- safe_k(base$temp_C_mean,            5)
k_sun   <- safe_k(base$sun_MJ_m2_mean,         5)
k_prec  <- safe_k(base$precip_mm_sum,          5)
k_shdi  <- safe_k(base$l_shdi,                 5)
k_cont  <- safe_k(base$l_contag,               5)
k_ed    <- safe_k(base$l_ed,                   5)
k_ai    <- safe_k(base$l_ai,                   5)
k_tree  <- safe_k(base$treeage,                5)

5.4 The model

model <- pfr(
  yield_tha ~
    lf(W_swf, argvals = grid, bs = "ps", k = 15) +      # (1) surrounding landscape
    s(distance_to_tree_strip, bs = "tp", k = k_dist) +   # (2) intrinsic variation
    s(fert_N,         bs = "tp", k = k_fertN) +    # thin plate regression splines
    s(temp_C_mean,    bs = "tp", k = k_temp) +
    s(sun_MJ_m2_mean, bs = "tp", k = k_sun) +
    s(precip_mm_sum,  bs = "tp", k = k_prec) +
    s(l_shdi,         bs = "tp", k = k_shdi) +
    s(l_contag,       bs = "tp", k = k_cont) +
    s(l_ed,           bs = "tp", k = k_ed) +
    s(l_ai,           bs = "tp", k = k_ai) +
    s(treeage,        bs = "tp", k = k_tree) +
    crop_unified +
    s(field, bs = "re"), # random effects 
  data   = base,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(model)

##     bs = "tp", k = k_fertN) + s(temp_C_mean, bs = "tp", k = k_temp) +

Term-by-term rationale:

  • lf(W_swf, argvals = grid, bs = "ps", k = 15) - the surrounding landscape term. Estimates a smooth coefficient function beta(distance) over the 100-1000 m domain using a penalized B-spline (bs = "ps") basis; k = 15 is generous relative to the 10 observed distances but is fine because the roughness penalty (chosen by REML) controls the effective wiggliness, not k itself.
  • s(distance_to_tree_strip, bs = "tp", k = k_dist) - intrinsic variation. A thin-plate smooth lets yield respond nonlinearly to proximity to the tree strip, consistent with the competition-zone literature (Swieter et al. 2019). I THINK HERE ONE CAN JUST TAKE A LOG SMOOTH THERE IS NO INDICATION THAT THESE EFFECTS ARE NON LINEAR SO I WOULD TAKE THEM LINEARLY The block of s(..., bs = "tp", k = ...) terms for fert_N, climate normals, and landscape-configuration indices represents field design as smooth (not necessarily linear) scalar effects.
  • crop_unified - parametric factor; crop identity has a large, roughly additive effect on yield and does not need smoothing.
  • s(field, bs = "re") - random intercept for field, absorbing unmodelled, field-specific variation and acknowledging that observations within a field are not independent.

6 Model Validation and Verification

6.1 Basis dimension check (k-index)

gam.check(model)

## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Look at the k-index column: a value well below 1 together with a low p-value for a given smooth means k may be too small (the smooth is being forced to be smoother than the data support) and should be increased (subject to safe_k’s ceiling); values around/above 1 are fine.

6.2 Residual diagnostics

res <- residuals(model)
fit <- fitted(model)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(fit, res, main = "Residuals vs fitted", xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residuals")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
hist(res, main = "Residual distribution", xlab = "Residuals")
qqnorm(res); qqline(res, col = "red")
# plot(base$distance_to_tree_strip, res,
#      main = "Residuals vs distance_to_tree_strip",
#      xlab = "distance_to_tree_strip", ylab = "Residuals")
# abline(h = 0, col = "red")
# par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

Check specifically for: (i) trumpet/fan shape in residuals-vs-fitted (heteroscedasticity, possibly by crop - consider s(fitted, by = crop_unified)-style variance modelling or a Gamma/log-link family if present); (ii) heavy tails in the Q-Q plot (consider a robust family or investigate the flagged outliers from Section 2.1); (iii) any remaining pattern of residuals against distance_to_tree_strip or fitted values, which would indicate the smooth is under- or over-fitting.

6.3 Residuals by field and by year (checks the random-effect structure)

# resid_df <- base |> mutate(resid = res)
# 
# ggplot(resid_df, aes(x = field, y = resid)) +
#   geom_boxplot() +
#   geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "red") +
#   theme_bw() +
#   labs(title = "Residuals by field") +
#   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
# 
# ggplot(resid_df, aes(x = factor(year), y = resid)) +
#   geom_boxplot() +
#   geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "red") +
#   theme_bw() +
#   labs(title = "Residuals by year", x = "year")

If residuals still show a systematic offset by field, s(field, bs = "re") is not fully doing its job (often because of the concurvity issue described next) and the fixed effects should be simplified. A systematic pattern by year suggests adding a year term.

6.4 Concurvity (the GAM analogue of collinearity)

Given that several field design smooths are near-constant within a field (Section 2.4), expect high concurvity between those terms and s(field, bs = "re"). full = FALSE shows pairwise concurvity and helps identify which specific pair of terms is problematic. If concurvity between, e.g., s(temp_C_mean) and s(field) is high, report this explicitly and consider the simplified model discussed in 01_model_choice_rationale.txt (Section 2) as a robustness check.

6.5 Influence / leave-one-field-out sensitivity

# refit dropping each field once, compare beta(distance) for W_swf
fields <- levels(base$field)
loo_coefs <- lapply(fields, function(f) {
  m <- update(model, data = base[base$field != f, ])
  coef(m, n = length(grid))
})

With only 8 fields, a leave-one-field-out refit is cheap and directly answers “is the estimated surrounding-landscape effect (or the distance-to-tree-strip effect) driven by a single field?” - important given the concurvity concerns above. Compare the estimated beta(distance) curve (and its confidence band) across the 8 refits, e.g. by overlaying coef(m, n = ...) for each fold.

6.6 Reported fit statistics

summary(model)$r.sq
## [1] 0.7532343
summary(model)$dev.expl
## [1] 0.7622408
AIC(model)
## [1] 2782.801

Report adjusted R^2, deviance explained, and REML/AIC alongside the diagnostics above - a high R^2 (as in the current model, ~0.76) is not by itself evidence that the model is correctly specified if concurvity is high; the diagnostics in this section are what establishes that.

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)
library(ggplot2)

W_swf <- df |>
  dplyr::select(id, distance, prop_swf) |>
  unique() |>
  filter(distance %in% c(100, 500, 1000)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = distance, values_from = prop_swf, names_prefix = "swf_") |>
  arrange(id)

pca_data <- df |>
  distinct(id, yield_tha, distance_to_tree_strip, crop_unified) |>
  inner_join(W_swf, by = "id") |>
  na.omit()

pca_res <- PCA(pca_data |> select(-id),
                quali.sup = which(names(pca_data |> select(-id)) == "crop_unified"),
                quanti.sup = which(names(pca_data |> select(-id)) == "yield_tha"),
                graph = FALSE)

get_eigenvalue(pca_res)
##       eigenvalue variance.percent cumulative.variance.percent
## Dim.1  1.6501266        41.253165                    41.25316
## Dim.2  1.1731086        29.327716                    70.58088
## Dim.3  0.8335961        20.839901                    91.42078
## Dim.4  0.3431687         8.579218                   100.00000
ind_coord <- as.data.frame(pca_res$ind$coord[, 1:2])
colnames(ind_coord) <- c("Dim1", "Dim2")
ind_coord$yield_scaled <- as.numeric(scale(pca_data$yield_tha))
ind_coord$crop_unified <- pca_data$crop_unified

var_coord <- as.data.frame(pca_res$var$coord[, 1:2])
colnames(var_coord) <- c("Dim1", "Dim2")
var_coord$label <- rownames(var_coord)

scale_f <- 0.8 * max(abs(ind_coord[, 1:2])) / max(abs(var_coord[, 1:2]))

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = ind_coord,
             aes(x = Dim1, y = Dim2, color = yield_scaled, shape = crop_unified),
             size = 2.5) +
  geom_segment(data = var_coord,
               aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = Dim1 * scale_f, yend = Dim2 * scale_f),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")), color = "black") +
  geom_text(data = var_coord,
            aes(x = Dim1 * scale_f * 1.1, y = Dim2 * scale_f * 1.1, label = label),
            size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_gradient2(low = "#2c7fb8", mid = "#ffffbf", high = "#d7191c",
                         midpoint = 0) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Dim1", y = "Dim2", color = "yield_scaled", shape = "crop") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

swf_long <- df |>
  dplyr::select(id, field, distance, prop_swf) |>
  unique()

swf_wide <- swf_long |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = distance, values_from = prop_swf) |>
  arrange(id)

grid <- as.numeric(names(swf_wide)[-c(1, 2)])
Y_swf <- as.matrix(swf_wide[, -c(1, 2)])
field_id <- df |> distinct(id, field) |> arrange(id) |> pull(field)

swf_model <- pffr(
  Y_swf ~ s(field_id, bs = "re"),
  yind = grid,
  data = list(Y_swf = Y_swf, field_id = factor(field_id)),
  family = binomial()
)

summary(swf_model)
## 
## Family: binomial 
## Link function: logit 
## 
## Formula:
## Y_swf ~ s(field_id, bs = "re")
## 
## Constant coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)  -3.1107     0.1226  -25.36   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Smooth terms & functional coefficients:
##                          edf Ref.df Chi.sq p-value    
## Intercept(yindex)  9.312e-04      9    0.0  <2e-16 ***
## s(field_id,yindex) 1.814e+01     18  123.6  <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## R-sq.(adj) =  0.564   Deviance explained = 52.6%
## -REML score = 630.95  Scale est. = 1         n = 11710 (1171 x 10)
## Sandwich correction (cluster) applied to covariance matrices.
plot(swf_model)

fitted_swf <- fitted(swf_model)
rownames(fitted_swf) <- swf_wide$id

W_smooth <- fitted_swf[match(id_order, rownames(fitted_swf)), ]

base$W_swf <- W_smooth

model <- pfr(
  yield_tha ~
    lf(W_swf, argvals = grid, bs = "ps", k = 15) +
    s(distance_to_tree_strip, bs = "tp", k = k_dist) +
    s(fert_N,         bs = "tp", k = k_fertN) +
    s(temp_C_mean,    bs = "tp", k = k_temp) +
    s(sun_MJ_m2_mean, bs = "tp", k = k_sun) +
    s(precip_mm_sum,  bs = "tp", k = k_prec) +
    s(l_shdi,         bs = "tp", k = k_shdi) +
    s(l_contag,       bs = "tp", k = k_cont) +
    s(l_ed,           bs = "tp", k = k_ed) +
    s(l_ai,           bs = "tp", k = k_ai) +
    s(treeage,        bs = "tp", k = k_tree) +
    crop_unified +
    s(field, bs = "re"),
  data   = base,
  method = "REML"
)

summary(model)
